text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A 20-year-old student is shot dead by police in Nairobi housing estate.
- Eagerly-awaited long rains spread to parched areas of Kenya.
- Mombasa police arrest three robbery suspects after a three-hour stakeout and a dramatic sea chase.
- Opposition Democratic Party leader Mwai Kibaki says the general election will be held in November.
- The PTA Bank, relocated to Nairobi from Burundi, is accused of mismanaging millions of dollars belonging to member states.
- Kenya's police commissioner says measures have been taken to ensure no incident happens again similar to the killing of 80 people in northern Kenya by bandits.
- Cash-strapped Nairobi city council is considering hiking the city water levy by more than 400 percent.
- The government receives overwhelming support for its decision to send troops and paramilitary police to repulse a cross-border incursion by bandits from Ethiopia.
- The government warns stern measures will be taken against any official found misappropriating 4,000 metric tonnes of seeds donated to farmers in drought-stricken areas. ($1=55 Kenyan Shillings)
